text:
maria: Heads up — nightly perf job flagged a 15-25% regression on the fused-paged path when running on SM90 (H100) with CUDA 12.2 vs SM80 (A100) CUDA 11.8. Probably kernel-selection or codegen spill.
eli: can you drop the bench numbers and a short profiler snippet? :eyes:
maria: sure. quick table from the harness (seq=2048, batch=1, kv-prefetch enabled):
```
kernel             | sm80 (11.8) | sm90 (12.2) | delta
fused-paged (cuda) | 1.00 ms     | 1.27 ms     | +27%
flashx (triton)    | 0.98 ms     | 1.08 ms     | +10%
paged-kv-hit rate   | 92%         | 70%         | -22pp
end-to-end latency  | 1.12 ms     | 1.40 ms     | +25%
```

maria: nvprof counters show a lot more L2 evictions and regspill on SM90 run. snippet: 
```
GPU: h100-s90
SM_efficiency: 87%
L2_write_bytes: 1.2GB -> 2.4GB
register_spill: 0.4MB -> 1.6MB
warp_stalls_mem: +18%
```

sam: ugh. could be that our CUDA-fallback path picks a scalarized kernel on SM90 because of new ISA/ptx mismatch. the triton kernels look more stable. we saw this in a different variant last quarter.
jin: fwiw i reproduced locally on a single H100 dev box. when seq>1024, the JITed cuda fused-paged chooses the small-warps codepath that spills. lowering block-size avoids spill but reduces occupancy.
eli: interesting — does the runtime choose different kernels based on compute capability heuristics? we have selector rules in selectors/attention_selector.py right?
maria: yes. current rule: prefer cuda_fused_paged for sm>=80, unless triton flagged. but selector doesn't consider register pressure or CUDA driver version. seems SM90+CUDA12.2 needs different preference.
ops-bot: nightly-run: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/runs/2026-03-14/1918876000 (artifact attached)
benchmark-bot: perf-diff: https://bench.redwood/compare/1918876 (summary: fused-paged sm90 regressed vs sm80)
eli: quick mitigation — add a runtime guard: if cuda_version >= 12.2 && arch == sm90 && seq >= 1024 -> prefer triton_flashx or fallback to flashx-triton kernel. can we A/B that in canary? :thinking:
sam: also look at batching heuristics — observed many small iteration batches because kv cache warmup had race with batching timeout. small batches amplify regspill costs.
jin: repro command I used: 
```bash
USE_TRITON=0 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./bench_attention --model=gpt-like --seq=2048 --batch=1 --profile nvprof
```
Changing USE_TRITON=1 drops the regression ~12% on SM90.
maria: i pushed a quick patch that changes selector priority and adds a driver-version check: selectors/attention_selector.py diff: 
```diff
- if arch >= 80: prefer('cuda_fused_paged')
+ if arch >= 80:
+     if arch == 90 and cuda_version >= '12.2': prefer('triton_flashx')
+     else: prefer('cuda_fused_paged')
```

eli: nice. can we also log when selector overrides default so we can track canary? add telemetry counter selector_override=true with reason.
ops-bot: deployed selector patch to canary cluster (region: us-west2) at 1918876600. watch for regressions.
maria: after canary deploy numbers look promising — latency back to ~+8% instead of +25% in the worst case. KV hit-rate also improved because triton kernel does less prefetch thrash.
sam: follow-ups: 1) add microbench for regspill to our kernel-ci 2) add selector tests covering (arch, cuda_version, seq) matrix 3) revisit batching heuristic: try accumulate_until_tokens=3 or timeout_ms=25 to avoid tiny batches on cold KV.
jin: i can take batching heuristic. i'll open PR with traces and perf numbers.
eli: i'll own selector telemetry + kernel-ci microbench. maria can you draft a postmortem / notes for the eng-runtime channel with the root cause and fixes?
maria: on it. TL;DR: SM90+CUDA12.2 codegen increased register pressure for our cuda_fused_paged variant at long seq lengths causing spills -> L2 thrash -> higher latency. Mitigation: prefer triton_flashx on SM90 until codegen/kernel is tuned; tune batching to avoid micro-batches.
:thumbsup:
